title: Haircut scaling branch keyed on payout<totalPrincipal rather than _isUnderwater
description: The scaling branch in migrateOut is keyed on the predicate payout<totalPrincipal (line 341) as a proxy for the pool being underwater, rather than an explicit _isUnderwater check. Standard ERC4626 redeem rounding favoring the vault can leave payout a few wei below totalPrincipal on an at-par/healthy pool, entering the scaling path and applying a negligible dust haircut that is stranded as protocol-owned dust. This is a predicate/spec-accuracy observation, not an exploit.
impact: Sub-wei / dust haircut on an at-par or healthy pool. The dust remains protocol-owned. No meaningful value at risk and no availability impact.
attackPath: 1. Pool is at-par/healthy but ERC4626 redeem rounds DOWN in the vault's favor.
2. payout ends up a few wei below totalPrincipal.
3. payout < totalPrincipal predicate (line 341) is true despite the pool not being economically underwater.
4. Scaling loop applies a sub-wei haircut; the dust remains protocol-owned.
recommendation: Gate the scaling branch on an explicit _isUnderwater determination (or apply a dust tolerance) so that rounding-induced sub-wei shortfalls on healthy pools do not enter the haircut-distribution path. Note: the dust impact overlaps the documented known issue 'Integer-division dust rounds DOWN (protocol favor)'; only the predicate-accuracy framing is novel. Submit only if that framing is judged additive.
